brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Michigan, and who represents you there.

head.title: What district am I in? Find your Michigan district — districtry
head.description: Click a point in Michigan — or search an address — and see your U.S. House, Michigan Senate, Michigan House and county, and who represents you.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Michigan, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Michigan — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search a Michigan address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 13 congressional districts — the largest districts Michigan carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app. The layer's own district field is CD120: TIGERweb rolled from the 119th Congress to the 120th, and a query naming the retired CD119 field is rejected outright (HTTP 400, measured 2026-09-03).

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Michigan Senate District
layers.rank_note: 38 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Michigan Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: mi-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI — the Open States current-people export (name, party, e-mail, personal site) merged with the Michigan Senate's own all-senators directory, which publishes a Capitol phone, e-mail, office building and contact page for all 38 seats. Open States carries no capitol address or phone for any Michigan legislator (measured 0 of 148), so that contact block comes entirely from the Senate's own directory.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 83 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: None yet — identity only. Michigan's county boards of commissioners are elected by district, and the state publishes every county's commissioner districts (with the commissioner's own name and party) as a single statutory filing under MCL 46.404/46.405; that is this instance's flagship layer and ships in its own change rather than being half-joined here. The card names the county and claims nothing about who runs it.

layers.label: Michigan House District
layers.rank_note: 110 House districts — the finest political tiling this instance ships today

source.answers: The Michigan House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: mi-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Open States current-people export (name, party, e-mail, personal site) — all 110 seats. NO CAPITOL CONTACT BLOCK SHIPS FOR THE HOUSE, and that is a measurement rather than an omission: Open States carries no capitol phone or address for any Michigan legislator, and house.mi.gov could not be reached from this project's build environment (TLS: "unable to get local issuer certificate", with the egress proxy's CA bundle explicitly supplied, while senate.michigan.gov answers 200 on identical flags). Whether that is the House site's own incomplete certificate chain or an artifact of this sandbox is unresolved and carries one CI-side probe before it is recorded as anything more — see mi/WATCH.md.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 514 unified (K-12) districts covering all but 27 pockets of the state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 469 km2 mean feature area, the largest of the four fabric layers this phase adds

source.answers: The unified (K-12) school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 514 features for Michigan, measured 2026-09-04

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Michigan school boards are elected (MCL 380.11a et seq.), and no statewide roster of the ~540 boards' members was found in the research pass — recorded as gap mi-school-board-members rather than guessed at. Per-district rosters are later phase work.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide. Together with the 27 elementary districts this tiles the state; the two never overlap.

layers.label: School District (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: 27 districts that operate no high school of their own, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 350 km2 mean feature area, though the mean is pulled well above the 45 km2 median by Bois Blanc Pines, whose district takes in a large area of Lake Huron

source.answers: The elementary school district covering the point, in the 27 places Michigan runs one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 27 features for Michigan, measured 2026-09-04. Layer 1 (SECONDARY) returns ZERO features for Michigan and is a recorded drop, not an empty toggle — see docs/DATA_LAYER_GUIDEBOOK.md

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER — the same gap as the unified layer (mi-school-board-members); the card names the district only.
source.applies: Michigan — the 27 districts that operate no high school of their own. These are GAP-FILLS, not overlays: measured 2026-09-04 at all 27 TIGER interior points, the unified layer returns nothing, and at every unified district's interior point this layer returns nothing. Shipping unified alone would answer 'no school district' to everyone living in one of the 27.

layers.label: County Commissioner District
layers.rank_note: 619 districts across all 83 counties — the finest tiling this instance ships, smaller than a state House district

source.answers: The county commissioner district covering the point, its county, and the population it was apportioned on.

boundary.label: Michigan Department of State, Bureau of Elections — "2021 County Commissioner Districts", the statewide compilation of the plans county apportionment commissions file under MCL 46.401-46.405; all 83 counties in one service, pre-built and shipped with the app. Its AGO item states the licence outright: "This dataset is a public record and ... there are no restrictions on the use, reproduction, or distribution of this dataset." (The Hub SITE item carries a separate CC-BY-SA; that is the site application, not this dataset, and its share-alike is not inherited.) The layer is named for its 2021 adoption year, labelled 2022 by the state's own viewer for the first election held under it, and backed by a feature class called CCD_2022_Edit — three names, one layer.

source.people: NONE, and that is a measurement rather than an omission. The source carries a Commissioner and Party on every one of its 619 polygons, which looks like a free roster and is not one: the item's own description says the values were "derived from the canvased November 2024 election results", so the column is a list of CERTIFIED ELECTION WINNERS, not of officeholders. That is why it is 100% filled — a district always has a winner — and the fill rate is evidence against maintenance, not for it. Measured 2026-09-03 across 12 counties read district-by-district against their own board pages (123 districts) plus ~40 more in a second pass: 93.5% named the right person, and every single miss ran the same direction, the layer naming the 2024 winner and the county naming their replacement. Wayne County District 5 still names a commissioner who died on 10 June 2025. Four further rows misspell a real surname. So the names are dropped at the build rather than shipped with a caveat, and the honest route to Michigan commissioner names — each county's own board page — is a later change with its own weekly refresh. Recorded as gap mi-commissioner-roster.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide, all 83 counties, 619 districts. Every Michigan county elects its commissioners by single-member district (MCL 46.401-46.405); none elects at large, so a polygon is the honest surface everywhere.

layers.label: Township or City
layers.rank_note: 1,581 records tiling the state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 1,122 general-law townships, 118 charter townships, 301 city placeholder records for 281 distinct cities (18 of which cross a county line), and 40 'not defined' records that are pure Great Lakes water

source.answers: The township covering the point, or the Census placeholder record for the city that stands in place of one — and which of the two it is.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / county subdivisions, layer 1, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 1,581 features for Michigan, measured 2026-09-04

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD SAYS SO. Michigan townships elect a supervisor, clerk, treasurer and trustees (MCL 41.61; MCL 42.3 for charter townships), and no statewide roster of them was found in the research pass — recorded as gap mi-township-officers. The card names the office and states plainly that this app does not know who holds it. The 301 city records and the 40 water records are Census bookkeeping constructs, not governments, so no roster claim applies to them at all.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide, all 1,581 records. The charter/general-law distinction is read from TIGER's own NAME suffix rather than a second source, so it cannot go stale against the name printed above it: measured 2026-09-04, the four LSADC values yield exactly four suffixes across 1,581 of 1,581 records.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,010 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas covering Michigan, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 139.7 km2 mean feature area, between a township and a precinct

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='26' — and the envelope must be Esri's own {xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax} shape, since passing this instance's {minLng,...} METRO_BBOX makes TIGERweb answer HTTP 200 with a JSON error envelope and zero features (measured 2026-09-04)

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more than it does.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide. 1,010 ZCTAs sit east of longitude -87.60; the fetch envelope returns 2,000 because Michigan's bounding box runs west across Lake Michigan to the far end of the Upper Peninsula, and even a clipped box still catches Chicago's 60628 since its south-west corner is in Illinois. NO RECTANGLE ISOLATES MICHIGAN — the same interlocking-states fact metros.json records about the fleet hand-off box — so neighbouring states' ZIPs appear in the map overlay, exactly as they do in Iowa's and Wisconsin's. The CARD is unaffected: it answers from a point query, so a reader always gets the ZCTA they are standing in.

layers.label: City Council District
layers.rank_note: Detroit's seven districts over 139 sq mi and Grand Rapids's three wards over 45 — both smaller than a typical Michigan ZCTA and far larger than a precinct; ranked on the larger city's districts

source.answers: Which city council or commission district you live in, in the two Michigan cities that publish their own boundaries — Detroit's seven council districts and Grand Rapids's three commission wards — and who represents you in it.

boundary.label: City of Detroit — "Detroit City Council Districts 2026", from the city's own ArcGIS org, pre-built and shipped with the app. THE CITY PUBLISHES FOUR COUNCIL-DISTRICT BOUNDARY SERVICES and their names do not settle which is in force: one titled "Current" dating from 2016, one named for 2026, one named for 2013 that was CREATED in December 2025, and NewDistrictBoundariesOption6, which reads like a rejected draft and is the same plan redigitised (99.575% point agreement, measured) — it is the one whose own description names the adoption. The plan was approved by the Council on 2024-02-06 and took effect on 2026-01-01, both stated in this service's own description. The builder decides it by measurement — "Current" carries geometry identical to the 2026 service and different from the 2013 one, and against Census 2020 blocks the shipped plan runs 87,393-94,820 against a 91,302 ideal (worst 4.28%) where the archived plan runs 78,966-100,623 (13.51%), which is what a plan drawn on the 2010 census looks like now. Both comparisons are gates in both directions. The seven districts sum to 639,111 — Detroit's Census 2020 population exactly — so they tile the city with no block double-counted or missed. The item carries no licenceInfo and is shared public by the city.

City of Grand Rapids — "Boundaries - City of Grand Rapids Wards" (CGR_Wards), from the city's own ArcGIS org, pre-built and shipped with the app. THE CITY PUBLISHES EIGHT WARD SERVICES AND NONE IS A NEWER PLAN, measured 2026-09-05 by sweeping all 681 of the org's feature services rather than the first 100 (which is how an earlier version of this note said two). Three are 100.000% identical to what ships, one differs only at the perimeter, and three are SINGLE wards rather than rival plans — each agreeing with its own shipped ward. The build gates on the one sibling that has tracked this service byte for byte. THE CURRENCY QUESTION WAS REAL AND IS ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT: the geometry was last edited 2018-01-24, before the census it is checked against, while the item description claims it is "maintained to reflect the most current adopted ward configuration". Michigan's own 2026 voting-precinct layer assigns each of the city's 59 precincts to a ward (20/20/19), and dissolved by that column it agrees with these polygons on 99.575% of 4,000 points — two independent publishers drawing the same three lines, so 2018 means unchanged rather than stale. That comparison is a gate. Against Census 2020 the three wards run 64,400-68,716 on a 66,328 ideal (worst 3.60%). Unlike Detroit the population identity is NOT exact and is not claimed to be: 21 of 2,883 blocks fall on one side of the ward outline and the other side of the Census place outline, a +66 difference against 198,917, which is two digitisations of one city edge. The item's licence is a use agreement conditioning use on carrying the city's disclaimer; the card quotes the sentences of that agreement that describe the DATA, in the city's own words and order rather than paraphrasing them, with the one cut (its two acceptance sentences, addressed to whoever accesses the data rather than to a reader) marked by an ellipsis. The builder ASSERTS every segment of that quotation against the live licenceInfo on each run, so a reworded agreement fails the build rather than leaving the card quoting words the city has stopped saying.

source.people: The nine members of Detroit's City Council, from the council's own page at detroitmi.gov — seven by district and two at large, per the 2012 charter Art. 4 §4-101. THE LIVE PAGE REFUSES THIS CLIENT: detroitmi.gov sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge on both the plain and the client-hints rungs, and this project does not defeat a challenge, so the roster is read from the Internet Archive's copy of that same page — the fleet's terminal fetch rung, in weekly use for Kendall and McHenry since 2026-07 — and the card states which day's copy it read. A snapshot older than 45 days is refused rather than served. NO PER-MEMBER phone or e-mail ships: neither the listing nor a member's own profile page carries a single mailto: or tel: link, measured on both, and that absence is the gap detroit-council-contact. The BODY's own office does ship — City Council Office, 2 Woodward Ave. Suite 1340, (313) 224-3443, published once for the whole Council — rendered for the body under the switchboard rule rather than attached to any member. mvic.sos.state.mi.us is challenged the same way; data.detroitmi.gov is NOT (it answers 200 with a readable robots.txt, and an earlier version of this note said otherwise on the strength of one substring match). Detroit's Legistar is abandoned since 2017 and never carried a district in OfficeRecordTitle even while maintained, where Milwaukee's carries "3rd District" in that same field — test a vendor by content per city, never by its name; its Persons table also flags all 45 records active, five of them system accounts. GRAND RAPIDS: the city's own City Commission pages, which are readable — www.grandrapidsmi.gov answers 200 and its robots.txt permits /government/ — so there is no archive hop here. The city states its own arithmetic ("This legislative body consists of the Mayor and six Commissioners... The residents of each Ward directly elect two commissioners"), and publishes SIX of those seven seats: one Ward 1 commissioner where Wards 2 and 3 each have two. THAT SEAT IS VACANT AND THE CITY SAYS SO OFF THE COMMISSION PAGE — its news post of 2026-04-17 states the vacancy "was created following the resignation of former Commissioner Drew Robbins"; an earlier version of this note said the city stated nothing, having measured only the commission page. No city source found states how the vacancy was resolved, so the card names the vacancy and its cause and stops there. The roster carries `seats` and `seatsPerWard` beside its members and a `vacancies` map KEYED BY WARD, so the card accounts for the seventh seat rather than concealing it or inventing a name — the Alexander County machinery, used here for the first time on a districted body. The cause is data, not prose: it was a ward-agnostic string literal in the card at first, on a row that fires for any ward short of its seats, so a later Ward 2 or 3 vacancy would have rendered Ward 1's predecessor by name on the wrong card. A ward that is short with no verified cause gets the neutral sentence instead, which stays true whatever caused it. Each member's own page supplies their ward, e-mail and direct phone; THE E-MAIL DOMAIN IS grcity.us AND NOT THE WEBSITE'S, so a scraper keyed to the site's own hostname finds none. 616.456.3000 is on every member's page and is the city switchboard, DETECTED as the number common to all of them and hoisted to the body rather than hardcoded.
source.applies: Detroit and Grand Rapids only — the two Michigan cities that publish their own council boundaries. Outside both the layer hides itself.

layers.label: Precinct
layers.rank_note: 3,895 voting precincts across all 83 counties, pre-built from the state's own 2026-cycle layer — 38.8 km2 mean feature area against a 6.4 km2 median, a six-fold skew because a rural township precinct and a city precinct are barely the same kind of object; the finest tiling this instance ships

source.answers: The voting precinct covering the point, its county, and how many voters were registered in it for the 2026 cycle.

boundary.label: Michigan Dept. of State, Bureau of Elections — "2026 Voting Precincts" (ArcGIS Online item c349bc2bb6c2468594d341a09f520ea8, the CURATED item: it carries the title, the licence, the validation caveat and the full field names). 3,895 features, pre-built by mi/scripts/build_mi_precincts.py (paged, Visvalingam-simplified, 2,000-point agreement gate). THE NEWEST MAP IS NOT ON THE MAPSERVER THAT CARRIES THE COMMISSIONER LAYER: that service publishes a precinct layer per cycle and stops at 2024, while the 2026 map lives on the state's ArcGIS Online org on a different host — and Michigan consolidated 4,340 precincts into 3,895 between the cycles, so building from the MapServer would have shipped a map 445 precincts wrong

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER — a precinct elects nobody; it is the unit a ballot is counted in. AND NO POLLING PLACE, which here is a fact about the source rather than a decision: the layer carries no polling field at all, so unlike Iowa's precinct builder there is nothing to decline. The card names the state's own caveat instead — the Bureau collects this from local election officials and says validation was "done by most, but not all" jurisdictions — and points a reader at their clerk.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide, all 3,895 precincts across all 83 counties, as drawn for the 2026 election cycle. Every precinct's county-subdivision key resolves against the Census MCD fabric this instance ships (1,530 of 1,530 distinct keys, measured 2026-09-04 — the same 1,530 on the 2024 map, because the consolidation happened WITHIN municipalities rather than between them), so the precinct and the Township or City card agree on which local government a point sits in. The state's voting-equipment column is deliberately not fetched: it changes on a different clock from the boundary.

layers.label: City or Village
layers.rank_note: 533 incorporated places, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 281 cities and 252 villages, small dense pockets inside the township fabric, so the smallest layer this instance ships at a 12 km2 mean

source.answers: The incorporated city or village covering the point, if any — and which of the two it is, because in Michigan that changes what else governs the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / incorporated places, layer 4, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 533 features for Michigan, measured 2026-09-04

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD SAYS SO — no statewide source names Michigan's mayors, village presidents, council members or clerks; the Michigan Municipal League's directory is membership-facing and the state publishes no aggregate. Recorded as gap mi-municipal-officeholders. Per-municipality rosters are later phase work, the route every other instance took.
source.applies: Michigan — statewide, all 533 incorporated places. A CITY is independent of any township; a VILLAGE remains part of one, so a village resident has two general-purpose local governments and each card names the other. Measured 2026-09-04: all 252 villages land inside a township at their TIGER interior point (235 general-law, 17 charter), zero exceptions, and the Census's own place class codes agree — every village is C1, 'does not serve as a county subdivision equivalent'.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: 1,290 police-station points in Michigan's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, ranked with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest police station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the same paged loader the post-office layer introduced (no builder script, no committed data/app file). Public domain. 1,290 points in Michigan's envelope, every one carrying name, address, city, state and ZIP, measured 2026-09-04 — under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Michigan — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes (608 of the 1,290 are in Michigan; the rest Wisconsin 396, Illinois 265, and a handful in Indiana, Ohio, Iowa and Minnesota). THIS IS A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers a 911 call at a given point is a service-area question, a separate concept this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest stations are and never who polices you. The intro says so in the reader's own sentence.

layers.label: Fire & EMS Station
layers.rank_note: 2,838 fire and EMS station points in Michigan's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, ranked with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest fire and EMS station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 51 (Fire Stations/EMS Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader the post-office layer introduced. Public domain. THIS IS THE LAYER THAT PAGING EXISTS FOR: 2,838 points in Michigan's envelope against the service's 2,000-record cap, and the cap is NOT an error — a single request returns HTTP 200 with exactly 2,000 rows and exceededTransferLimit set, silently dropping 838 real stations. Measured 2026-09-04: paged it is two requests and 2,838, every one carrying name, address, city, state and ZIP. Fire and EMS are one layer because USGS publishes them as one, named 'Fire Stations/EMS Stations'

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a fire station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Michigan — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes (1,406 of the 2,838 are in Michigan; the rest Wisconsin 798, Illinois 578, and a handful in Indiana, Iowa, Ohio and Minnesota). A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which department or ambulance service is dispatched to a point is a service-area question, a separate concept this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest stations are and never who responds. The intro says so in the reader's own sentence.

layers.label: Post Office
layers.rank_note: 1,799 post-office points in Michigan's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, so it is ranked last with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest post offices to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 38 (Post Offices), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope (no builder script, no committed data/app file). Public domain. 1,799 points in Michigan's envelope, every one carrying name, address, city, state and ZIP, measured 2026-09-04. THE FETCH PAGES: the service caps a response at 2,000 records and returns HTTP 200 with exceededTransferLimit rather than an error, so a single request is safe only by margin — Michigan is at 1,799 and its fire-station sibling is at 2,838, already over

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a post office is a federal facility, not an elected district. The card answers where the nearest ones are, not who runs them.
source.applies: Michigan — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. Of the 1,799 points, 900 are in Michigan and the rest are in Wisconsin (535), Illinois (334) and a handful in Iowa, Ohio, Indiana and Minnesota. THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT SPILL: nearest-3 is a proximity fact rather than a jurisdictional claim, so for a reader in Menominee the nearest post office really is across the river in Wisconsin, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: the Michigan State Capitol, downtown Lansing (Ingham County)

negative_point.note: downtown Toledo, Ohio — south of the Michigan line and inside permalink_gate's minLat (41.55), so the point is still selectable; measured to miss all five ANCHOR layers (phase 3's four live TIGERweb fabric layers are deliberately not anchors — anchors are pre-built and election-stable)

geometry.note: The whole-Michigan-state outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from all 83 counties' TIGERweb State_County layer-1 geometry by mi/scripts/build_metro_outline.py (METRO_COUNTY_FIPS = every county; DISPATCH_COUNTY_FIPS empty — no layer is county-keyed yet). Michigan is 2-band coverage: every layer answers statewide, so there is no wider region band. It dissolves to ONE ring, 1,716 vertices — TIGERweb's county fabric is WATER-INCLUSIVE (Keweenaw County alone spans 2.57 degrees of longitude, out past Isle Royale), so the two peninsulas and every Great Lakes island tile continuously through county water rather than sitting apart. A mid-lake point therefore reads inside coverage, which is correct — that water is assigned to Michigan counties — and is why the negative point is on land in Ohio rather than out on the water.
Every county, pre-built from TIGERweb State_County layer 1.
U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb Legislative layer 0 (field CD120 — the 120th Congress; CD119 is retired and its query 400s).
Michigan Senate districts, pre-built by mi/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).
Michigan House districts, pre-built by mi/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).

All 619 county commissioner districts across all 83 counties, pre-built by mi/scripts/build_mi_commissioner_districts.py from the Bureau of Elections' statewide compilation (2,000-point agreement gate at 100.00%, per-county 1..N numbering check, MCL 46.401(1) 5..21 board-size check, and a guard that REFUSES the file if the source's Commissioner/Party columns ever reach data/app/). 611 of 619 carry an apportionment population; Baraga District 1 and all seven Cheboygan districts do not, and the card omits the row rather than showing a blank.

2026-cycle voting precincts, mi/scripts/build_mi_precincts.py. Exact band, not a floor: the builder refuses to write any count but 3,895, because on a cycle-scoped layer a count change is real information (Michigan went 4,340 -> 3,895 between the 2024 and 2026 maps) rather than drift.

Detroit's seven City Council districts, mi/scripts/build_mi_detroit_council.py. Exact band: the council's district seats are fixed at seven by the city charter, so any other count is a source change wanting a human, not drift.
Grand Rapids's three City Commission wards, from the city's own ArcGIS org. Built by mi/scripts/build_mi_grand_rapids_wards.py, whose currency gate is the state's own 2026 precinct layer.

Warren's five council wards, from the city's own ArcGIS account (item snippet "Approved 1/10/2023 Updated Labels 4-30-24"), built by mi/scripts/build_mi_warren_wards.py. THE WARD LAYER IS AT SERVICE INDEX 32, not 0 — a hardcoded /0 returns HTTP 200 with no features key and dies with a KeyError that reads like an outage; the builder reads the FeatureServer root and asserts the layer's name. The item states NO terms and is shared public (the Detroit case, not Lansing's CC BY-NC), and the builder REFUSES to rebuild if the city ever adds a licence, so geometry is never republished under terms nobody has read. Currency is measured, not assumed: dissolved by the state's own 2026 precinct WARD column (53 precincts, 10/10/11/11/11) the wards agree on 99.550% of 4,000 sampled points. The five wards tile the city EXACTLY — 139,387 against the Census place's 139,387 with zero blocks on the wrong side, Detroit's identity rather than Grand Rapids's bounded edge disagreement — and balance runs -2.46% to +3.78% on Census 2020.

Flint's nine council wards, effective 2 August 2022, built by mi/scripts/build_mi_flint_wards.py. THE SERVICE NAMES ARE ALL BUT INVERTED and nothing here is decided by a name: the plan in force is service `Wards22` (whose AGO item is titled "Wards23"), while `Wards2022` is the 2012 plan (its item honestly titled "City of Flint - Old Wards") and `Wards_Outline`, published by the city's own account, is also 2012. All three carry nine features called Ward 1..Ward 9; the currency gate separates them by twenty-three points — 99.525% for the shipped layer against 76.9% for both old ones. The item states no terms and is shared public, and the builder refuses to rebuild if that changes. The nine wards are the most evenly drawn in the fleet: -0.30% to +0.39% on Census 2020, 81,242 against the Census place's 81,252 across ten edge blocks.

Battle Creek's five commission wards, from the City of Battle Creek's own ArcGIS org, built by mi/scripts/build_mi_battle_creek_wards.py. The item states no terms and is shared public (the Detroit/Warren/Flint case). Currency measured against the state's own 2026 precinct WARD column (13 precincts, 2/2/3/3/3) at 99.450%; balance -4.09% to +4.18% on Census 2020, 52,706 against the Census place's 52,721 across 12 edge blocks. THE LAYER CARRIES A COMMISSIONER NAME PER WARD AND NONE OF THEM SHIP: four of five records were last edited in March 2023, Michigan cities elect in odd Novembers, and the city's own commission page answers 403 — a name field is not a roster.

history_page.intro: districtry Michigan answers for all 83 counties: the county commissioner districts Michigan's own Bureau of Elections compiles from every county's apportionment filing, plus the national tier every U.S. state can serve from national publishers. It was built dark across three changes in one day — the national tier, the commissioner flagship, then publication — rather than going live on arrival.

entries.title: Grand Rapids, and what a 2018 file had to prove
entries.body: Grand Rapids became the second Michigan city this app answers for, and its arrival changed how Detroit is served too: one toggle now covers both cities rather than each getting its own, which is how this project adds places without adding clutter. Links people already shared for Detroit keep working. The city divides itself into three wards and elects two commissioners from each, plus a mayor chosen by the whole city — seven people, and the city says so in its own words on its own page. Six of those seven are published. One ward lists a single commissioner where the others list two, and the city does not say why, so the card tells you a seat is unlisted rather than quietly showing you one name where there should be two. The map behind it needed proving. The city's ward boundaries were last edited in 2018, and a file that old could easily be a map of somewhere that has since been redrawn — the page describing it says it is current, but a description is not evidence. The state of Michigan publishes its own list of voting precincts for the 2026 election, and it records which ward each of Grand Rapids's fifty-nine precincts belongs to. Drawn from that instead, the wards come out in the same three shapes, agreeing almost everywhere: two organisations, working seven years apart, drawing the same lines. So the 2018 date means nothing has changed, and the map is current. That check now runs every time the boundaries are rebuilt, and refuses if the two ever stop agreeing. One thing is stated rather than smoothed over: the wards and the Census Bureau's outline of the city disagree very slightly about where the city edge runs — about twenty blocks and sixty-six people out of nearly two hundred thousand. That is two careful organisations tracing one line, not an error in either, and it is recorded rather than rounded away.

entries.title: Detroit's council districts, and the route that was never walked
entries.body: Detroit became the first city this app answers for in Michigan: seven City Council districts, drawn from the city's own published boundaries. Which boundaries took some deciding — the city publishes four competing versions and their names do not settle which is in force, so the choice was made by arithmetic instead. The plan that ships divides Detroit's people almost evenly on the 2020 census; the one it replaced is out by three times as much, which is what a map drawn on the 2010 census looks like ten years later. A fourth version, whose name reads like a rejected draft, turned out to be the very same lines drawn at a coarser resolution, and it is the one that names the dates: the Council adopted this plan on 6 February 2024 and it took effect on 1 January 2026. The card first shipped naming your district and nobody in it, on the finding that every route to the council's membership was closed. Two of those five findings were wrong. The city's open-data portal was called blocked when it answers perfectly well — a conclusion drawn from searching a page for the word "challenge" while the server was plainly saying yes. And the route this project already uses every week for two Illinois counties, reading a public archive of a page whose live version refuses us, was never tried at all. It answers with all nine members. So the card now names your council member, and the two members every Detroiter elects citywide, and tells you which day's archived copy it read. A copy older than 45 days is refused rather than shown to you. No phone number or e-mail appears, and that is the city's doing rather than ours: it publishes none, on the council listing or on any member's own page. That absence is recorded as a gap, in the same place as every other thing this app cannot yet tell you.

entries.title: Published
entries.body: Michigan went live at districtry.com/mi/, the fleet's sixth instance. Publishing an instance that had been built in the dark turned up four defects the whole test battery had been green on, and three were the same shape — a claim nothing compared against the thing it claimed. This app's font files had never been copied into its own folder, so all eighteen of them would have 404'd and the page would have quietly rendered in whatever typeface your device chose; its preview image, named in three places, did not exist either. Its sources page still carried Iowa's identity in every tag a search engine reads, because it was cloned from Iowa and only the generated parts were ever regenerated. An unused helper left over from that clone made the fleet's privacy page state that one Michigan layer sends your exact selected point to a government server, which no Michigan layer does. And Michigan's own map bounds, which run out into Lake Michigan because the state's counties do, reached far enough west to claim Chicago. All four are fixed, and two new checks now watch for their kind: every file a page asks for must exist, and every page must say which page it is.

entries.title: County commissioner districts
entries.body: The layer Michigan was chosen for: all 619 county commissioner districts across all 83 counties, from the Bureau of Elections' own statewide compilation of the plans counties file under MCL 46.401-46.405. Every Michigan county elects its commissioners by single-member district, so every reader in the state gets a district. The card names the district, its county and the population it was apportioned on — and not the commissioner. The state's layer does carry a name per district, but it lists the winners of the November 2024 election rather than whoever holds the seat now: checked against the counties' own board pages it is 93.5% right, every error runs the same direction, and one district still names a commissioner who died in June 2025. Naming people from it would have been easy and wrong, so this app says what it knows and records the rest as a gap.

entries.title: Arrived
entries.body: Four layers, statewide, each with a sourced boundary: county (83), U.S. House (13), Michigan Senate (38) and Michigan House (110). Both chambers and the U.S. House delegation carry a weekly-refreshed roster; the county card names the county and claims nothing about who runs it, because Michigan's commissioner districts ship as their own change rather than half-joined here. The congressional boundary is the first in the fleet built against TIGERweb's 120th-Congress layer — the retired CD119 field now 400s outright.
